declared_question: For real compounds with a measured IC50 against both CYP3A4 and CYP2D6, does apparent inhibition of one enzyme predict the other, and what does a claim of 'this compound inhibits CYP' risk collapsing when it does not name the enzyme, the assay and the document behind it?
relation_to_sibling_protocol: This reuses, unmodified, the admission rule already established by labs/chembl_egfr/protocol.json (chembl37-egfr-representation-v1): exact IC50 in nM, standard_flag 1, potential_duplicate 0, no data validity comment, molecule_chembl_id equal to parent_molecule_chembl_id, an RDKit-valid structure, and pChEMBL consistent with standard_value to within 0.011. It reads two whole targets rather than two named assays, because unlike the EGFR case, a single CYP target's IC50 record set is itself spread across many independent assays and documents; that spread is part of what this protocol teaches, not a nuisance to average away silently.

entity.structure: RDKit canonical isomeric SMILES from the ChEMBL parent record

label_contract.parent_aggregation: median across every admitted activity for that parent under that target

overlap_contract.definition: A parent admitted under both targets. 'Shares a document' means at least one contributing activity for each target cites the same document_chembl_id. A 'clean single pair' additionally requires exactly one admitted activity per target for that parent, so its two pChEMBL values are not a median over multiple studies on either side.
overlap_contract.correlation: Pearson r and Spearman rho, computed once over the full overlap and once over the clean single-pair subset only, as a robustness check of each other. No fitted model of any kind is used anywhere in this protocol.

excluded_by_design: transporters, induction, metabolite identification and clinical drug-drug-interaction outcomes: this protocol reads only in vitro IC50 inhibition records
any causal or clinical claim: an in vitro potency difference is not a prospective interaction risk statement for any named drug pair
any correction for cross-study heterogeneity beyond the same-document 'clean pair' comparison already declared above
